To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) in the presence of protective cover, vigilance in groups is reduced by the mere presence (dilution) of companions and this can be explained by the scramble for cover; 2) the dilution game is affected by the speed of predator approach, the speed of food intake and the rate at which cover can be reached.

(i) the mere presence of other individuals in a group, without the need to consider collective detection, can cause a decrease in vigilance levels; (ii) the decrease in vigilance is caused by a scramble to reach protective cover; (iii) this scramble is more intense in smaller groups; (iv) the scramble can be reduced by a high rate of food intake; and (v) the scramble is less intense when predator evasion is more effective

(1) foraging in groups is risky, (2) the risk of predation can be reduced by using protective cover, (3) foragers can reduce the risk of predating by using protective cover and (4) the use of protective cover by individuals reduces the risk of predatation on the whole group.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of dilution in antipredatory vigilances.
the mechanisms by which vigilance is regulated in groups of foraging animals.
how the behaviour of animals is influenced by their social environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(i) vigilance is a costly behavior; (ii) the costs of vigilance can be reduced in the presence of protective cover and/or in groups; (iii) the costs of maintaining high levels of personal vigilance are greater in large groups; (iv) individuals can reduce their vigilance to reach cover faster, but this behavior is more costly in small groups.
vigilance in groups can be reduced by the mere presence and proximity of companions, even when these are not engaged in collective detection.
vigilance in groups is not simply about collective detection but is influenced by a range of factors that can be captured by the concept of dilution
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vigilance levels are reduced in groups because individuals can take advantage of numerical risk dilution.
the presence of companions in a group can reduce vigilance, but the effect of group size is mediated by the cost to vigilance and the cost of predation.
vigilance is a costly activity and that the costs of vigilance can increase with group size.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dilution game can be a mechanism that causes a reduction in vigilence with group size in the presence of protective cover.
the mere presence of a companion can reduce predation risk and that this can lead to changes in vigilence with group size.
vigilance can decrease with group size when foragers can take cover.
